fields.meta_title: Cake Order Form Builder for Bakers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a cake order form that turns a guest count into a cake size and holds the date with a deposit. Every order lands in a table you own.
fields.h1: Build a Cake Order Form Your Kitchen Can Bake From
fields.hero_description: Describe your cakes and the notice each one needs. Emergent builds the cake order form with its prices and saves every order to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Cake Order Form Needs to Ask
fields.features_subheading: A cake is made for one date and one crowd. These six parts get the details in writing before anyone turns on the oven.
fields.feature_1:
Notice periods set per cake type

Give cupcakes 2 days of notice and a three-tier cake 3 weeks. The date picker grays out every date sooner than that, and nobody can book a fondant cake for tomorrow morning.
fields.feature_2:
Guest counts turned into a pan size

Ask how many people the cake has to feed and suggest the pan from your own serving chart. Customers stop guessing between an 8-inch and a 10-inch round on their own.
fields.feature_3:
Flavors priced as the customer picks

List each sponge and filling once with its upcharge beside it. The total updates with every pick, and the order row keeps each choice for the baker who mixes the batter.
fields.feature_4:
Inspiration photos saved with the order

Add an upload field for a picture of the cake the customer has in mind. The decorator opens it from the kitchen ticket instead of scrolling back through a text thread.
fields.feature_5:
Deposits that hold the pickup date

Connect Stripe and take a deposit when the order is placed. The date stays held once the deposit clears, and each order row shows the balance the customer still owes at pickup.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can hand to a developer

Publish the form on your bakery's domain or embed it in your menu page. Export the code to GitHub when a developer adds a loyalty program or a sync with your cash register.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Bakeries and the Orders They Take
fields.tab_content_1:
With 25 guests, the form suggests a 10-inch round

Parents planning a party at Larkspur Bakery start with the guest count, not a pan size. The form follows Wilton's serving chart. A 9-inch round serves 24, one short. It suggests a 10-inch round instead: 28 servings for 25 guests. The customer picks a chocolate sponge and pays $48 for a Saturday pickup.
fields.tab_content_2:
All 70 guests fit on three tiers

Fernhill Cake Studio books weddings months ahead. A couple enters 70 guests and gets a quote for 6, 8 and 10 inch tiers, which Wilton's chart puts at 74 wedding servings. A $150 deposit holds the date. Until it is paid, the date shows as pending and other couples can still ask for it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each gluten-free order waits for Tuesday

Gluten-free cakes at Juniper Street Bakery are baked on Tuesday, first thing, before any wheat flour comes out. A customer who picks the gluten-free sponge pays $8 more, and the form offers pickup on Wednesday or later. The kitchen ticket prints the allergy note in red at the top.
fields.tab_content_4:
By 6 am Friday, Saturday's bake list is written

Oakmont Bakeshop's head baker once added up order tickets by hand. Now the form keeps the count. At 6 am every Friday it posts Saturday's bake list to the #kitchen channel in Slack. Cakes are grouped by sponge and size. This week it lists 4 vanilla 8-inch, 3 chocolate 9-inch and 2 lemon 6-inch cakes, 9 in all.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Cake Order Form
fields.howto_description: Settle your menu and your notice periods first. The prompt is short once those are on paper.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the notice for each cake
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Price the upgrades and the deposit
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the cakes on your menu and the sizes each comes in: rounds, sheets, tiers, cupcakes by the dozen. Note the base price of each size. Anything you only make on request can sit in a free-text field instead of on the menu.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A guest count is easier for customers than a pan size. Write down how many servings each pan gives at the slice size you cut, and the form can turn the number of guests into a suggested cake.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Count the days a cake takes before pickup, decorating time included. That count is the shortest notice you accept. Add the days you open for pickup and any dates the shop is closed.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put a price on each upgrade: a filling, a fondant finish, a second tier, a gluten-free sponge. Then set the deposit as a flat amount or a share of the total, and decide when the rest is due.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your menu, serving chart, notice periods and prices into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form with its price logic and the orders table behind it. Ask for changes the same way, such as a new flavor.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send the bake list to the kitchen
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide when the kitchen needs its list and where the team reads it, such as a Slack channel. Ask for orders grouped by sponge and size, and each batch of batter will cover every cake that needs it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Order a cake as a customer would
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter a guest count, try a date inside your notice period, then pick an allowed one and pay the deposit with a test card. Check that the orders table shows the right size and price, then delete the test row.

plan.angle: The live SERP is printable sheets (Etsy, Amazon pads, Pinterest), bakeries' own inquiry forms and two builder template galleries. None of them handles what makes cake orders hard for a baker: turning a guest count into a pan size, refusing dates inside the notice period a decorated cake needs, keeping allergy requests off the regular bake, and adding up the week's orders into one bake list. This page answers the PAA questions bakers' customers ask (lead time, servings, the 4 Day Cake Rule) and shows four bakeries using the form to settle each one.
tab_stories: A birthday customer types 25 guests and the form recommends a 10-inch round, which Wilton's chart puts at 28 party servings, before they pick a flavor.
A wedding couple expecting 70 guests gets a three-tier quote of 6, 8 and 10 inch tiers worth 74 wedding servings, and a $150 deposit holds their date.
A customer who picks a gluten-free sponge pays $8 more and the order moves to the bakery's Tuesday gluten-free bake, with the note printed in red on the kitchen ticket.
Every Friday at 6 am the week's orders roll up into one Saturday bake list by sponge flavor and size, posted to the kitchen's Slack channel.
